subject: math
title: Combinations of Transformations: Translations, Reflections and Rotations
seo_title: Grade 7 Math: Combinations of Transformations Worksheets (Free, BC Curriculum, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on combinations of transformations for the BC curriculum: translate points and shapes, reflect them in the x- and y-axis, rotate them 90° and 180° about the origin, combine steps in order and name the transformation that maps one shape onto another. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: Move every vertex with the same rule. In a combination, do the steps in order.
key_sub: Translation: right and up add, left and down subtract. Reflection in the x-axis changes the sign of y; in the y-axis, the sign of x. Rotation about the origin: 90° clockwise (x, y) → (y, −x), 90° counterclockwise (−y, x), 180° (−x, −y).
body_html:
Three ways to move a shape

A transformation moves a shape on the Cartesian plane. The shape keeps its size. The new shape is called the image. Grade 7 uses three kinds:

TransformationWhat it doesRule for (x, y)
Translationslides the shapeadd or subtract: (x + a, y + b)
Reflection in the x-axisflips it up or down(x, −y)
Reflection in the y-axisflips it left or right(−x, y)
Rotation of 90° clockwiseturns it a quarter turn(y, −x)
Rotation of 90° counterclockwiseturns it a quarter turn the other way(−y, x)
Rotation of 180°turns it a half turn(−x, −y)

All rotations here are about the origin, (0, 0). Move every vertex with the same rule, then join the new vertices.

Translations

Right adds to x and left subtracts from x. Up adds to y and down subtracts from y.

Example

Translate (−2, 4) 5 units right and 7 units down.

x: −2 + 5 = 3. y: 4 − 7 = −3.

Answer: (3, −3)

Example

Describe the move from (−3, 2) to (4, −1).

New minus old. x: 4 − (−3) = 7, so 7 units right. y: −1 − 2 = −3, so 3 units down.

Answer: 7 units right and 3 units down

Reflections in the axes

The axis is the mirror line. In the x-axis, the sign of y changes. In the y-axis, the sign of x changes. Each image is the same distance from the mirror as the shape.

Example

Reflect (−4, 5) in the x-axis.

x stays −4. y changes sign: 5 → −5.

Answer: (−4, −5)

Rotations about the origin

For a quarter turn, swap the two numbers, then change one sign. Clockwise: change the sign of the second number. Counterclockwise: change the sign of the first number. For a half turn (180°), change both signs.

Example

Rotate (2, 5) 90° counterclockwise about the origin.

Swap: (5, 2). Change the sign of the first number: (−5, 2). Check: (2, 5) is in Quadrant I, and a counterclockwise quarter turn takes it to Quadrant II.

Answer: (−5, 2)

Combinations of transformations

Do the steps one at a time, in the order given. The image of the first step is the starting point for the next. The order matters: changing it can give a different answer.

Combination

Translate (−4, 2) 3 units right, then reflect it in the y-axis.

Step 1: x: −4 + 3 = −1, so (−1, 2). Step 2: change the sign of x, so (1, 2). Doing the steps the other way round gives (4, 2), then (7, 2): a different point.

Answer: (1, 2)

Which transformation?

Which single transformation maps (3, −5) to (−3, 5)?

Both signs changed and the numbers stayed in the same order. That is a half turn.

Answer: a rotation of 180° about the origin

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Translating the wrong wayRight and up add; left and down subtract
Changing x for an up or down moveUp and down change only y
From −6 to 1 doing 6 − 1 = 5New minus old: 1 − (−6) = 7
Reflecting in the wrong axisIn the x-axis, y changes sign. In the y-axis, x changes sign
Rotating the wrong wayClockwise goes the way clock hands move: from the top to the right
Only swapping the numbers in a 90° turn: (3, 1) → (1, 3)Swap and change one sign: (1, −3) clockwise, (−1, 3) counterclockwise
Doing a combination in the wrong orderDo the first step, then use its image for the second step

faq.q: What do Grade 7 students learn about transformations in BC?
faq.a: In the BC Grade 7 curriculum (Geometry and measurement), students perform and describe combinations of transformations: translations, reflections in the axes and rotations about the origin, using coordinates in all four quadrants.

faq.q: How do you reflect a point in the x-axis or the y-axis?
faq.a: In the x-axis, keep x and change the sign of y: (4, 1) becomes (4, −1). In the y-axis, keep y and change the sign of x: (4, 1) becomes (−4, 1).

faq.q: How do you rotate a point 90° about the origin?
faq.a: Swap the two numbers, then change one sign. For 90° clockwise, (x, y) becomes (y, −x); for 90° counterclockwise, it becomes (−y, x). A 180° turn changes both signs.

faq.q: Are transformations on the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: The Grade 7 FSA numeracy assessment is based on the BC curriculum and asks students to apply math to real problems. Practising transformations builds the coordinate and spatial reasoning skills those problems use.

items.q: Translate (3, −2) 6 units left. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 6 units left: x: 3 − 6 = −3, y stays −2. (3, −2) → (−3, −2).

items.q: Translate (−1, 4) 7 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 7 units down: x stays −1, y: 4 − 7 = −3. (−1, 4) → (−1, −3).

items.q: Translate (−5, −3) 8 units right. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 8 units right: x: −5 + 8 = 3, y stays −3. (−5, −3) → (3, −3).

items.q: Translate (−3, 2) 5 units right and 4 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 5 units right and 4 units down: x: −3 + 5 = 2, y: 2 − 4 = −2. (−3, 2) → (2, −2).

items.q: Translate (4, −1) 6 units left and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 6 units left and 3 units up: x: 4 − 6 = −2, y: −1 + 3 = 2. (4, −1) → (−2, 2).

items.q: Translate (−2, −5) 7 units right and 4 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 7 units right and 4 units up: x: −2 + 7 = 5, y: −5 + 4 = −1. (−2, −5) → (5, −1).

items.q: Translate (5, 3) 3 units left and 7 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 3 units left and 7 units down: x: 5 − 3 = 2, y: 3 − 7 = −4. (5, 3) → (2, −4).

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units right and 3 units down. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (−5, 2). Translate 6 units right and 3 units down: x: −5 + 6 = 1, y: 2 − 3 = −1. (−5, 2) → (1, −1). That is point B. Point C moves the wrong way up or down, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units left and 3 units up. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (4, −2). Translate 6 units left and 3 units up: x: 4 − 6 = −2, y: −2 + 3 = 1. (4, −2) → (−2, 1). That is point D. Point B moves the wrong way up or down, and point C comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units left and 2 units down. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (3, 4). Translate 5 units left and 2 units down: x: 3 − 5 = −2, y: 4 − 2 = 2. (3, 4) → (−2, 2). That is point A. Point C moves the wrong way up or down, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: A point moves from (−3, 2) to (4, −1). Describe the translation.
items.e: Find the change: new minus old. x: 4 − (−3) = 7, so 7 units right; y: −1 − 2 = −3, so 3 units down. The translation is 7 units right and 3 units down. The move crosses the y-axis, so the sizes add: 3 + 4 = 7.

items.q: A point moves from (5, −4) to (−1, 2). Describe the translation.
items.e: Find the change: new minus old. x: −1 − 5 = −6, so 6 units left; y: 2 − (−4) = 6, so 6 units up. The translation is 6 units left and 6 units up. The move crosses the y-axis, so the sizes add: 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: A point moves from (−2, −6) to (−6, 1). Describe the translation.
items.e: Find the change: new minus old. x: −6 − (−2) = −4, so 4 units left; y: 1 − (−6) = 7, so 7 units up. The translation is 4 units left and 7 units up.

items.q: Triangle B is a translation of triangle A. Describe the translation.
items.e: Pick one vertex and its image. The corner (−5, 2) moves to (1, −3). x: 1 − (−5) = 6, so 6 units right. y: −3 − 2 = −5, so 5 units down. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: A translation is written as (x, y) → (x − 4, y + 2). Describe it in words.
items.e: x − 4 makes x smaller by 4, so the point moves 4 units left. y + 2 makes y bigger by 2, so it moves 2 units up.

items.q: Which rule shows a translation 5 units right and 3 units down?
items.e: Right adds to x: x + 5. Down subtracts from y: y − 3. So (x, y) → (x + 5, y − 3).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A (−4, 1), B (−1, 1) and C (−1, 5). It is translated 3 units right and 6 units down. What are the vertices of the image?
items.e: Add 3 to every x and subtract 6 from every y. A: (−1, −5). B: (2, −5). C: (2, −1).

items.q: After a translation 4 units left and 5 units up, the image of point A is (−1, 2). Where was point A before the move?
items.e: Undo the move: go 4 units right and 5 units down. x: −1 + 4 = 3. y: 2 − 5 = −3. A was at (3, −3). Check: 4 left and 5 up from (3, −3) is (−1, 2).

items.q: Hana translates (−2, 4) 3 units down and gets (−5, 4). What mistake did she make?
c: She changed x instead of y
She moved up instead of down
items.e: Down changes only y: 4 − 3 = 1. The image is (−2, 1). Hana subtracted 3 from x, which moves the point left.

items.q: A point moves from (−6, −2) to (1, −2). How far did it move?
items.e: Only x changes. 1 − (−6) = 1 + 6 = 7, and it is positive, so the point moved 7 units right. (5 comes from 6 − 1: the move crosses the y-axis, so the sizes add.)

sets.title: Reflections in the x-axis and the y-axis

items.q: Reflect (5, −3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (5, −3) → (−5, −3).

items.q: Reflect (−2, 6) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−2, 6) → (−2, −6).

items.q: Reflect (4, 1) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (4, 1) → (4, −1).

items.q: Reflect (−6, −4) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−6, −4) → (6, −4).

items.q: Reflect (−1, −5) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−1, −5) → (−1, 5).

items.q: Reflect (2, 3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (2, 3) → (−2, 3).

items.q: Reflect (0, −5) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (0, −5) is on the y-axis (the mirror line), so it stays at (0, −5).

items.q: Reflect (−3, 0) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−3, 0) is on the x-axis, 3 units left of the y-axis. Reflect in the y-axis: x changes sign, −3 → 3. The image is 3 units right: (3, 0).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−3, 4). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−3, 4) → (−3, −4). That is point C. Point A is the reflection in the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (5, −2). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (5, −2) → (−5, −2). That is point A. Point B is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (−5, −2). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−5, −2) → (5, −2). That is point B. Point A is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: Triangle B is the reflection of triangle A. Which axis is the mirror line?
items.e: Compare a vertex and its image: (−5, 2) → (−5, −2). x stays the same and y changes sign, so the shape flipped up or down. The mirror line is the x-axis.

items.q: Triangle B is the reflection of triangle A. Which axis is the mirror line?
items.e: Compare a vertex and its image: (−2, −1) → (2, −1). y stays the same and x changes sign, so the shape flipped left or right. The mirror line is the y-axis.

items.q: A triangle has vertices (1, 2), (4, 2), (4, 5). It is reflected in the x-axis. What are the vertices of the image?
items.e: Reflect each vertex in the x-axis: keep the other coordinate and change the sign of y. (1, 2), (4, 2), (4, 5) → (1, −2), (4, −2), (4, −5).

items.q: A triangle has vertices (−5, −1), (−2, −1), (−2, −3). It is reflected in the y-axis. What are the vertices of the image?
items.e: Reflect each vertex in the y-axis: keep the other coordinate and change the sign of x. (−5, −1), (−2, −1), (−2, −3) → (5, −1), (2, −1), (2, −3).

items.q: The points (−5, 2) and (5, 2) are reflections of each other in which axis?
items.e: y stays 2 and x changes sign (−5 → 5), so the points flip left and right across the y-axis.

items.q: When you reflect a point in the y-axis, what changes?
items.e: The y-axis is a mirror standing up. The point flips left or right, so only x changes sign. Example: (3, 5) → (−3, 5).

items.q: Point (−3, −5) is reflected in the x-axis. Which quadrant is the image in?
items.e: The image is (−3, 5): x stays negative and y becomes positive. Left and up is Quadrant II.

items.q: Lucas reflects (4, −6) in the y-axis and gets (4, 6). What mistake did he make?
items.e: He changed the sign of y. That is a reflection in the x-axis. In the y-axis, x changes sign: (−4, −6).

items.q: Point Q is the reflection of point P in the x-axis. Q is at (−4, −1). Where is P?
items.e: Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of y, and reflecting back does the same. (−4, −1) → (−4, 1).

sets.title: Rotations of 90° and 180° about the origin

items.q: Rotate (2, 5) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (2, 5) → (5, −2).

items.q: Rotate (−3, 1) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−3, 1) → (1, 3).

items.q: Rotate (−4, −6) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−4, −6) → (−6, 4).

items.q: Rotate (5, −2) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (5, −2) → (2, 5).

items.q: Rotate (1, 3) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (1, 3) → (−3, 1).

items.q: Rotate (−6, 4) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−6, 4) → (−4, −6).

items.q: Rotate (3, −4) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (3, −4) → (−3, 4).

items.q: Rotate (−5, −1) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (−5, −1) → (5, 1).

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (5, 2). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (5, 2) → (2, −5). That is point D. Point A is a turn the wrong way, and point B only swaps the numbers.

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (−2, 4). Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−2, 4) → (−4, −2). That is point A. Point B is a turn the wrong way, and point C only swaps the numbers.

items.q: Point P is rotated 180° about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (3, −5). Rotate 180°: both signs change. (3, −5) → (−3, 5). That is point B. Points A and C change only one sign: those are reflections in an axis.

items.q: Triangle A is rotated about the origin to give triangle B. Describe the rotation.
items.e: Follow one vertex: (4, 2) → (2, −4). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (4, 2) → (2, −4). The shape turned a quarter turn clockwise about the origin.

items.q: Triangle A is rotated about the origin to give triangle B. Describe the rotation.
items.e: Follow one vertex: (5, −1) → (1, 5). Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (5, −1) → (1, 5). The shape turned a quarter turn counterclockwise about the origin.

items.q: Point (4, −1) is rotated about the origin and lands on (1, 4). Describe the rotation.
items.e: Try the rules. 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x), so (4, −1) → (1, 4). That matches. (90° clockwise would give (−1, −4).)

items.q: Point (−3, −2) is rotated about the origin and lands on (3, 2). Describe the rotation.
items.e: Both signs changed and the numbers stayed in the same order. That is a half turn: 180°.

items.q: Point (5, −3) is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Which quadrant is the image in?
items.e: (5, −3) is in Quadrant IV. A quarter turn counterclockwise moves it to the next quadrant counterclockwise: Quadrant I. Check: the image is (3, 5).

items.q: Point (−2, 6) is rotated 270° clockwise about the origin. Where does it land?
items.e: 270° clockwise is three quarter turns clockwise. That ends in the same place as one quarter turn counterclockwise (360° − 270° = 90°). Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−2, 6) → (−6, −2).

items.q: Chloe rotates (3, 1) 90° counterclockwise about the origin and gets (1, 3). What mistake did she make?
c: She swapped the numbers but changed no sign
items.e: A 90° turn swaps the numbers and changes one sign. Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (3, 1) → (−1, 3). (1, 3) is still in Quadrant I, so it cannot be a quarter turn.

items.q: A triangle has vertices (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 3). It is rotated 180° about the origin. What are the vertices of the image?
items.e: A 180° rotation changes both signs of every vertex: (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 3) → (−1, −1), (−4, −1), (−4, −3).

items.q: Which rotation about the origin always gives the same image as a rotation of 90° clockwise?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. Going 270° counterclockwise leaves 360° − 270° = 90° to go, so you end where a 90° clockwise turn ends.

items.q: Point (−2, 3): translate 5 units down, then reflect in the x-axis. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 5 units down: x stays −2, y: 3 − 5 = −2. (−2, 3) → (−2, −2). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−2, −2) → (−2, 2).

items.q: Point (4, −1): translate 6 units left, then reflect in the y-axis. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 6 units left: x: 4 − 6 = −2, y stays −1. (4, −1) → (−2, −1). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−2, −1) → (2, −1).

items.q: Point (1, 2): translate 3 units right and 4 units down, then reflect in the x-axis. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 3 units right and 4 units down: x: 1 + 3 = 4, y: 2 − 4 = −2. (1, 2) → (4, −2). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (4, −2) → (4, 2).

items.q: Point (−5, −3): translate 2 units right and 6 units up, then reflect in the y-axis. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 2 units right and 6 units up: x: −5 + 2 = −3, y: −3 + 6 = 3. (−5, −3) → (−3, 3). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−3, 3) → (3, 3).

items.q: Point (3, 4): translate 5 units left and 1 unit down, then reflect in the y-axis. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 5 units left and 1 unit down: x: 3 − 5 = −2, y: 4 − 1 = 3. (3, 4) → (−2, 3). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−2, 3) → (2, 3).

items.q: Point (2, −4): reflect in the x-axis, then translate 5 units left and 2 units up. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (2, −4) → (2, 4). Translate 5 units left and 2 units up: x: 2 − 5 = −3, y: 4 + 2 = 6. (2, 4) → (−3, 6).

items.q: Point (−3, 1): reflect in the y-axis, then translate 4 units left and 3 units down. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−3, 1) → (3, 1). Translate 4 units left and 3 units down: x: 3 − 4 = −1, y: 1 − 3 = −2. (3, 1) → (−1, −2).

items.q: Point (−4, 1): translate 3 units right and 2 units up, then rotate 90° clockwise about the origin. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 3 units right and 2 units up: x: −4 + 3 = −1, y: 1 + 2 = 3. (−4, 1) → (−1, 3). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−1, 3) → (3, 1).

items.q: Point (2, −5): translate 1 unit left and 3 units up, then rotate 180° about the origin. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Translate 1 unit left and 3 units up: x: 2 − 1 = 1, y: −5 + 3 = −2. (2, −5) → (1, −2). Rotate 180°: both signs change. (1, −2) → (−1, 2).

items.q: Point (3, 2): rotate 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translate 4 units right and 1 unit down. Where is the final image?
items.e: Do the steps in order. Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (3, 2) → (−2, 3). Translate 4 units right and 1 unit down: x: −2 + 4 = 2, y: 3 − 1 = 2. (−2, 3) → (2, 2).

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units down, then reflected in the y-axis. Which point is the final image?
items.e: Translate 5 units down: x stays −4, y: 2 − 5 = −3. (−4, 2) → (−4, −3). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−4, −3) → (4, −3). That is point C. Point B is the reflection in the wrong axis, and point D is only the translation.

items.q: Point P is translated 3 units right, then reflected in the x-axis. Which point is the final image?
items.e: Translate 3 units right: x: 1 + 3 = 4, y stays 3. (1, 3) → (4, 3). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (4, 3) → (4, −3). That is point A. Point C is the reflection in the wrong axis, and point D is only the translation.

items.q: Reflect (4, −3) in the y-axis, then reflect the image in the x-axis. Where does it land?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (4, −3) → (−4, −3). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−4, −3) → (−4, 3). Both signs changed.

items.q: A reflection in the x-axis followed by a reflection in the y-axis gives the same result as which single transformation?
items.e: The first reflection changes the sign of y and the second changes the sign of x. Both signs change, and that is exactly what a 180° rotation about the origin does. Example: (2, 5) → (2, −5) → (−2, −5).

items.q: A triangle has vertices (−4, 1), (−1, 1), (−1, 3). It is translated 2 units right and 4 units down, then reflected in the y-axis. What are the vertices of the final image?
items.e: Translate first: (−2, −3), (1, −3), (1, −1). Then reflect in the y-axis (change the sign of x): (2, −3), (−1, −3), (−1, −1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 3). It is rotated 180° about the origin, then translated 3 units up. What are the vertices of the final image?
items.e: Rotate first (change both signs): (−2, −1), (−5, −1), (−2, −3). Then add 3 to every y: (−2, 2), (−5, 2), (−2, 0).

items.q: Olivia must translate (−3, −5) 2 units up, then reflect it in the x-axis. She gets (−3, 7). What mistake did she make?
c: She translated down instead of up
items.e: Right order: Translate 2 units up: x stays −3, y: −5 + 2 = −3. (−3, −5) → (−3, −3). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−3, −3) → (−3, 3). Olivia did the steps the other way round: (−3, −5) → (−3, 5) → (−3, 7). The order of the steps matters.

items.q: A point is translated 3 units right, then reflected in the y-axis. The final image is (−1, 4). Where did the point start?
items.e: Work backwards and undo the last step first. Undo the reflection: (−1, 4) → (1, 4). Undo the translation (go 3 units left): (1, 4) → (−2, 4). Check: Translate 3 units right: x: −2 + 3 = 1, y stays 4. (−2, 4) → (1, 4). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (1, 4) → (−1, 4).

items.q: Ryan translates (1, 2) 3 units up, then reflects it in the x-axis. Liam reflects (1, 2) in the x-axis first, then translates it 3 units up. What do they get?
items.e: Ryan: Translate 3 units up: x stays 1, y: 2 + 3 = 5. (1, 2) → (1, 5). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (1, 5) → (1, −5). Liam: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (1, 2) → (1, −2). Translate 3 units up: x stays 1, y: −2 + 3 = 1. (1, −2) → (1, 1). The order of the steps changes the answer.

items.q: Point (−4, 2) is translated 6 units right, then reflected in the x-axis. Which quadrant is the final image in?
items.e: Translate 6 units right: x: −4 + 6 = 2, y stays 2. (−4, 2) → (2, 2). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (2, 2) → (2, −2). x is positive and y is negative: Quadrant IV.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Triangle B points the same way as triangle A: it only slid. That is a translation (6 units right and 5 units down). A reflection or a 180° turn would flip or turn the triangle.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (−2, 1) → (2, 1). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−2, 1) → (2, 1). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a reflection in the y-axis.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (5, 1) → (−5, −1). Rotate 180°: both signs change. (5, 1) → (−5, −1). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a rotation of 180°.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (−2, 1) → (1, 2). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−2, 1) → (1, 2). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a rotation of 90° clockwise.

items.q: Triangle PQR has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1), (5, 3). Its image has vertices (−2, 1), (−5, 1), (−5, 3), in the same order. Which single transformation was used?
items.e: Compare each vertex with its image. Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (2, 1) → (−2, 1). The rule works for every vertex, so it is a reflection in the y-axis.

items.q: Triangle PQR has vertices (−1, 2), (−1, 5), (−3, 5). Its image has vertices (2, 1), (5, 1), (5, 3), in the same order. Which single transformation was used?
items.e: Compare each vertex with its image. Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−1, 2) → (2, 1). The rule works for every vertex, so it is a rotation of 90° clockwise.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices (−3, 2), (−1, 2), (−1, 5). Its image has vertices (3, −1), (1, −1), (1, 2), in the same order. Which combination maps the triangle onto its image?
c: Reflect in the x-axis, then translate 3 units down
Translate 3 units down, then reflect in the x-axis
Reflect in the y-axis, then translate 3 units down
Reflect in the y-axis, then translate 3 units up
items.e: Test it on one vertex. Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−3, 2) → (3, 2). Translate 3 units down: x stays 3, y: 2 − 3 = −1. (3, 2) → (3, −1). The other vertices work the same way.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices (1, 2), (4, 2), (4, 4). Its image has vertices (4, −2), (1, −2), (1, −4), in the same order. Which combination maps the triangle onto its image?
c: Translate 5 units right, then rotate 180° about the origin
Reflect in the y-axis, then translate 5 units right
Rotate 180° about the origin, then translate 5 units left
Rotate 180° about the origin, then translate 5 units right
items.e: Test it on one vertex. Rotate 180°: both signs change. (1, 2) → (−1, −2). Translate 5 units right: x: −1 + 5 = 4, y stays −2. (−1, −2) → (4, −2). The other vertices work the same way.

items.q: A BC Ferries route is drawn on a grid map. A ferry leaves a terminal at (−5, −2) and sails 7 units right and 4 units up. Where does it arrive?
items.e: Translate 7 units right and 4 units up: x: −5 + 7 = 2, y: −2 + 4 = 2. (−5, −2) → (2, 2).

items.q: On a whale-watching trip near Victoria, Kai marks an orca on a grid map at (4, −3). Later the orca is at (−2, 1). Describe the orca’s move as a translation.
items.e: Find the change: new minus old. x: −2 − 4 = −6, so 6 units left; y: 1 − (−3) = 4, so 4 units up. The translation is 6 units left and 4 units up.

items.q: Leah draws a cedar tree beside a lake. The shoreline is the x-axis, and the top of the tree is at (−2, 5). She draws the tree’s reflection in the water. Where is the top of the reflection?
items.e: The water line is the x-axis, so reflect in the x-axis: x stays −2, y changes sign. (−2, 5) → (−2, −5).

items.q: Wei designs a logo for his school’s lacrosse team in Kamloops. One corner of the left half is at (−4, 3). He reflects it in the y-axis to make the right half, then translates the whole logo 2 units down to fit the T-shirt. Where is the image of that corner?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−4, 3) → (4, 3). Translate 2 units down: x stays 4, y: 3 − 2 = 1. (4, 3) → (4, 1).

items.q: Emma makes a quilt square for a class display. A triangle piece has a vertex at (1, 4). She rotates the piece 90° clockwise about the centre of the square (the origin) to place the next piece. Where is the vertex now?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (1, 4) → (4, −1).

items.q: Mei draws a pinwheel for a Terry Fox Run poster. One blade tip is at (2, 5). The opposite blade is the first one rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its tip?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (2, 5) → (−2, −5).

items.q: In a snowboarding video game, Ethan’s rider is at (−5, 4) on the screen grid. The rider jumps 6 units right and 7 units down, then the screen is flipped (reflected in the y-axis). Where is the rider now?
items.e: Translate 6 units right and 7 units down: x: −5 + 6 = 1, y: 4 − 7 = −3. (−5, 4) → (1, −3). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (1, −3) → (−1, −3).

items.q: In a coding app, Noah’s sprite is at (3, 2). He rotates it 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translates it 4 units right. Where does it end up?
items.e: Rotate 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (3, 2) → (−2, 3). Translate 4 units right: x: −2 + 4 = 2, y stays 3. (−2, 3) → (2, 3).

items.q: A game piece moves from (3, −5) to (−3, 5). Ava says it was a rotation of 180° about the origin. Harjot says it was a reflection in the x-axis, then a reflection in the y-axis. Who is right?
items.e: 180° rotation: both signs change, (3, −5) → (−3, 5). Two reflections: (3, −5) → (3, 5) → (−3, 5). Both give the same image.

items.q: In a board game, Mateo’s piece was translated 4 units up, then reflected in the x-axis. It ended at (2, −3). Where did it start?
items.e: Undo the steps in reverse order. Undo the reflection: (2, −3) → (2, 3). Undo the translation (4 units down): y: 3 − 4 = −1. The piece started at (2, −1). Check: Translate 4 units up: x stays 2, y: −1 + 4 = 3. (2, −1) → (2, 3). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (2, 3) → (2, −3).

items.q: A soccer coach in Surrey draws a play on a grid with the origin at the centre spot. A player at (−4, 2) runs 3 units right. Then the coach copies the play to the other side by reflecting it in the y-axis. Where is the player’s image?
items.e: Translate 3 units right: x: −4 + 3 = −1, y stays 2. (−4, 2) → (−1, 2). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−1, 2) → (1, 2).

items.q: Sofia plans a bike ride on a grid map of Stanley Park. From (−6, 1), she rides 5 units right and 3 units down, then 4 units right and 2 units up. Which single translation takes her from the start to the end?
items.e: Add the moves. x: 5 + 4 = 9, so 9 units right. y: −3 + 2 = −1, so 1 unit down. Check: (−6, 1) → (3, 0).
